title: Task/CalendarEvent query after/before are not LocalDateTime: tasks types them as UTCDate, calendars as String

## Task/CalendarEvent query after/before are not LocalDateTime: tasks types them as UTCDate, calendars as String
Crates: jmap-tasks-types, jmap-calendars-types
Evidence: draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33.txt:2209-2221 defines CalendarEvent/query `after`/`before` as LocalDateTime, interpreted in the `timeZone` argument. draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06.txt:1095-1098 says Task/query "is the CalendarEvent/query method". RFC 8984 §5.2.1 Task `due` is a LocalDateTime (tasks-types/src/task.rs:466-468 documents it as such). Yet tasks-types/src/task.rs:579-585 has `pub after: Option<UTCDate>` / `pub before: Option<UTCDate>`, "Task `due` date must be on or after this UTCDate". UTCDate requires a trailing Z (jmap-types/src/id.rs:226-243), so a spec-conforming LocalDateTime filter value fails to deserialize this deny_unknown_fields struct, and a client cannot send one. calendars-types/src/event.rs:401,406 uses `Option<String>` for the same fields. jmap_jscalendar_types::LocalDateTime (jscalendar-types/src/lib.rs:104) exists, and tasks-types already uses it for capability minDateTime/maxDateTime (tasks-types/src/capability.rs:56,62).
Why breaking later: Changing the type of public fields on a public filter struct is a semver break.
Fix: Type both siblings' after/before as Option<jmap_jscalendar_types::LocalDateTime>. While doing that, consider the same type for the scalar LocalDateTime properties still carried as String (event.rs:205 recurrence_id, :323 start; task.rs:385 recurrence_id, :468 due, :472 start), since jscalendar-types types the same properties as LocalDateTime.
Size: M

Votes: REAL: Only the tasks half of this holds up; the calendars half doesn't. Both crates are publishable (neither Cargo.toml sets publish = false), and a search for "LocalDateTime" and "after/before" found no existing bead.

The real part is in jmap-tasks-types. At HEAD, crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/task.rs:578-584 types the Task filter's after/before as Option<UTCDate>, documented as "Task `due` date must be on or after this UTCDate". The tasks half is a real break; the calendars half is weaker.

Tasks half, confirmed at HEAD:
- `crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/task.rs:579-585` declares `TaskFilterCondition.after/before: Option<UTCDate>`. The struct is at line 550, is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and the crate's Cargo.toml has no `publish = false`, so it is published.
- draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06.txt:1093-1096 says Task/query "is the CalendarEvent/query method".
- draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33.txt:2209-2221 defines that method's `after`/`before` as LocalDateTime, interpreted in the `timeZone` argument.; REFUTE: Refuted for both crates. The code does match the claim: crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/task.rs:579-585 has `after`/`before` as Option<UTCDate>, and crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/event.rs:401,406 has them as Option<String>. Neither one is a break that only a semver change could fix.
